newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine teachers strike for higher pay.
newsitem.headline: Argentine teachers strike for higher pay.

text.p: Argentine teachers staged a strike and protest marches on Friday for better pay and a higher education budget, adding to pressure on President Carlos Menem after recent protests against high unemployment.

Thousands of teachers and student supporters marched through the streets of Buenos Aires to a tent outside Congress, where state-sector teachers have been staging a hunger strike since April to demand higher salaries.
The teachers' union, CTERA, estimating that the average monthly wage for teachers is $300, is pushing for $500.
"This march is to defend state schooling; it's a fight which has the support of more and more Argentines every day," CTERA chief Marta Maffei said.
The union estimated that 90 percent of state sector teachers observed the strike, with many private school staff joining them in sympathy. There were no government figures on the size of the protest.

Menem acknowledged that his government "is in debt with teachers" and promised "miracles" to resolve the country's pay and employment situation. Education Minister Susana Decibe called it "a shame" that schools should close, but added: "The whole country would like to see teachers better paid."
